ITQAN:v2p415/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p415/r21.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p415/r21.claim: Du'a can mean asking or supplication.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268/r8.claim: The command to call and God's response are understood literally, with the response nonetheless subject to God's will.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268/r8.anchor: والظاهر حمل الدعاء والاستجابة على ظاهرهما، إلا أن الاستجابة مقيدة بمشيئة الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r1.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi reads the command as ‘ask Me and I will give you.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reads it as ‘obey Me and I will grant you.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r3.claim: A group including Mujahid takes calling as worship and response as reward for worship; this is supported by the following reference to those arrogant about worship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r3.anchor: ادعوني، اعبدوني وأستجب لكم، آتيكم على العبادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r4.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r4.claim: Al-Numan ibn Bashir reports the Prophet's statement that supplication is worship, followed by his recitation of this verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r4.anchor: روى النعمان بن بشير، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الدعاء هو العبادة»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the command as affirming God's oneness so that He will forgive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: وحدوني أغفر لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r6.speaker: الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r6.claim: Al-Thawri says that refraining from sins is itself supplication.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan urges people to act and hope, saying God is bound to answer believers who do good and grant them more of His bounty.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r7.anchor: اعملوا وأبشروا، فإنه حق على الله أن يستجيب للذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r8.speaker: أنس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r8.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's instruction to ask God for every need, even a sandal strap.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r8.anchor: ليسأل أحدكم ربه حاجته كلها حتى شسع نعله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r9.claim: The arrogant who refuse worship are understood as those who refuse supplication; ‘humiliated’ means abject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r9.anchor: إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي: أي عن دعائي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r10.claim: Most of the seven readers and several others read ‘they will enter’ actively; others read it passively, with disagreement about two readers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p268#2/r10.anchor: وقرأ جمهور السبعة، والحسن، وشيبة: سيدخلون مبنيا للفاعل

STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r9.claim: Divine aid to messengers ends with condemnation of those too arrogant to worship God, then transitions to God’s power over creation.
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r9.anchor: An affirmation of the Divine Aid that God sends upon His messengers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r6.claim: Verses 56–85 marshal arguments for monotheism and the Hereafter from within and around people, warn Quraysh, and firmly promise help to the Prophet and companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r6.anchor: The arguments in favour of monotheism and the Hereafter found within man and around him are referred to

IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r8.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r8.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r8.claim: Mujahid lists added yāʾs left unvowelled before a separate alif when attached to a jussive verb, including فاذكروني أذكركم and رب فأنظرني.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p152/r8.anchor: ومما ترك تحريك يائه عند الألف المقطوعة المتصلة بالفعل المجزوم قوله ﴿ فاذكروني أذكركم ﴾ البقرة 152

RAZI-FULL:v25p73#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p73#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p73#2/r8.claim: The servant address followed believers’ prayer: they invoked God in faith, and He answered by calling them His servants; unbelievers did not supplicate and were not included.
RAZI-FULL:v25p73#2/r8.anchor: هذا الخطاب حصل للمؤمن بسعيه بتوفيق الله ، وذلك لأن الله تعالى قال : { ادعونى أستجب لكم }

ASAD-NOTES:40:59#n43/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:59#n43/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:40:59#n43/r1.claim: Asad cross-references the promise to answer prayer with 2:186.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#4/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#4/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#4/r9.claim: In Ghafir, the discussion turns from prayer and God's favors, including night and day, to creation; thus “creator of everything” comes before “no deity but He.”
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r4#4/r9.anchor: فالكلام كما ترى على الخَلْق وعلى نعم الله وفضله على الناس لا على التوحيد فقدم الخلق لذلك

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p47/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p47/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p47/r1.claim: The surrounding passage concerns creation and God's blessings, not monotheism; creation is foregrounded accordingly, with each expression placed to fit its context.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p47/r1.anchor: فقدم الخلق لذلك فوضع كل تعبير في موطنه اللائق حسب السياق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p498/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p498/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p498/r1.claim: Ghafir discusses creation and God's blessings, including the creation of the heavens and earth, rather than focusing here on monotheism; accordingly, it foregrounds creation in its wording.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p498/r1.anchor: لا على التوحيد فقدم الخلق لذلك فوضع كل تعبير في موطنه اللائق حسب السياق

IBNHIBBAN:890/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:890/r1.speaker: author
IBNHIBBAN:890/r1.claim: Ibn Hibban classifies calling on God in every circumstance as worship through which one draws near to Him.
IBNHIBBAN:890/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الدعاء هو العبادة» ، ثم قرأ هذه الآية:

IBNHIBBAN:890/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:890/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNHIBBAN:890/r2.claim: Nuʿmān b. Bashīr reports the Prophet identifying supplication as worship and then reciting this verse as evidence.
IBNHIBBAN:890/r2.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الدعاء هو العبادة» ، ثم قرأ هذه الآية:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r4.claim: Here arrogance also carries the sense of evasion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r5.claim: After recalling the Hereafter, the passage turns to monotheism and direct prayer to God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r5.anchor: After reminding people of the Hereafter, a reminder is now sounded about monotheism

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r6.claim: God requires no intermediary: anyone may ask Him directly, which rejects the idolaters' belief that access to God depends on deities as intercessors.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r6.anchor: no means or intermediary is required to ask from Him

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r7.claim: God accepts every right supplication; when He delays or does not grant one, His wisdom makes the deferral good, so people should be content.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r7.anchor: the Almighty definitely accepts every right supplication. If He does not accept a supplication

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r8.claim: Only God has authority to accept or reject requests and knows the wisdom behind His actions; asking anyone else is useless.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p48/r8.anchor: It is totally useless to go to someone other than God for requests because it is only He Who has the authority to accept or reject requests

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p49/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p49/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p49/r1.claim: Those who arrogantly neglect worship despite God's open invitation will soon enter Hell in humiliation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p49/r1.anchor: those who are showing indifference in worshipping Him merely because of arrogance should remember that soon they will enter Hell in a humiliating way

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p49/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p49/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p49/r2.claim: The warning addresses the same opponents described in verse 56: political ambition and fear of inferiority, not doubt or argument, drive their evasion and lead to humiliation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p49/r2.anchor: Earlier in verse 56 it has been stated that those who are opposing Muḥammad (sws) are not doing so

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر وأبو عمرو في رواية عباس بن الفضل
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim through Abū Bakr, and Abū ʿAmr through ʿAbbās read with ḍamma on yāʾ, making the verb passive.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم في رواية أبي بكر، وأبو عمرو في رواية عباس بن الفضل: سيدخلون جهنم

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r2.speaker: الباقون وحفص عن عاصم وأبو عمرو في غير رواية عباس
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r2.claim: The remaining readers, Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, and Abū ʿAmr outside ʿAbbās’s transmission read with fatḥa on yāʾ, making the verb active.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وحفص عن عاصم وأبو عمرو في غير رواية عباس: سيدخلون بفتح الياء

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r3.claim: The active form is supported by commands to enter in 15:46 and 16:29; the passive derives from causative أُدخلوا, whose active counterpart takes two objects, as in 40:46.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r3.anchor: يدل على سيدخلون قوله: ادخلوها بسلام آمنين [الحجر/ 46] فادخلوا أبواب جهنم [النحل/ 29]

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r4.claim: The passive construction has one expressed object, indicating that its active causative counterpart takes two objects, as in أدخلوا آل فرعون أشد العذاب.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p114/r4.anchor: ألا ترى أن الفعل مبني للمفعول، وقد تعدى إلى مفعول واحد، فهذا يدل على أنه إذا بني للفاعل تعدى إلى مفعولين

NASHR:v2p251/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p251/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر ورويس
NASHR:v2p251/r4.claim: At the second occurrence in al-Muʾmin, the target of this segment, Ibn Kathīr, Abū Jaʿfar, and Ruways use passive yāʾ-damma and khāʾ-fatḥa; the other occurrence has separate reader details.
NASHR:v2p251/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو جعفر ورويس الحرف الثاني من المؤمن، وهو قوله سيدخلون جهنم كذلك

NASHR:v2p251/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p251/r5.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p251/r5.claim: The remaining readers use active yāʾ-fatḥa and khāʾ-damma in the five listed places, including the target verse.
NASHR:v2p251/r5.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الياء وضم الخاء في المواضع الخمسة

QIRAAT-ER:40:60:12#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:40:60:12#1/r1.speaker: Pss
QIRAAT-ER:40:60:12#1/r1.claim: The passive yudkhalūna means they will be made to enter or admitted, foregrounding imposed entry rather than active movement.
QIRAAT-ER:40:60:12#1/r1.anchor: Pss, mutawatir: "Canonical passive reading shifts the verb to ""they will be made to enter/admitted

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p182#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p182#6/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p182#6/r1.claim: The Prophet says supplication itself is worship and then recites this verse.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p182#6/r1.anchor: عن منصور والأعمش عن ذر عن يسيع الكندي عن النعمان بن بشير أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال إن الدعاء هو العبادة ثم قرأ

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p182#6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p182#6/r2.speaker: أبوه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p182#6/r2.claim: Ibn al-Taymi’s father says that if an iron shackle from Hell were placed on a mountain, it would crush it until it reached the black water.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p182#6/r2.anchor: أنا ابن التيمي عن أبيه قال لو أن غلا من أغلال جهنم وضع على جبل لوهصه حتى يبلغ الماء الأسود

MUSNAD-AHMAD:18352/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18352/r1.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18352/r1.claim: Al-Nu'man b. Bashir reports that the Prophet declared supplication to be worship and then recited this verse.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18352/r1.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، قال: " إن الدعاء هو العبادة "، ثم قرأ

MUSNAD-AHMAD:18386/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18386/r1.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18386/r1.claim: Al-Nu'man b. Bashir reports the Prophet's statement that supplication is worship, followed by his recitation of the full verse.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:18386/r1.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الدعاء هو العبادة "، ثم قرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, and others interpret call upon Me as worship Me, and I will answer as I will reward you for it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r1.anchor: أي اعبدوني أثبكم على ما روي عن ابن عباس والضحاك ومجاهد وجماعة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r2.speaker: سفيان الثوري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r2.claim: Asked to pray for someone, Sufyan al-Thawri said abandoning sins is prayer: spoken supplication expresses inward seeking and is valid only with genuine orientation and leaving disobedience; a sinner who persists is not truly asking even after a thousand invocations.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r2.anchor: الثوري أنه قيل له : ادع الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r3.claim: Al-Alusi says Sufyan's account supports interpreting supplication as worship, since abandoning sins is itself a major act of worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81/r3.anchor: وما ذكر مؤيد لتفسير الدعاء بالعبادة ومحقق له فإن ترك الذنوب من أجل العبادات

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r1.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r1.claim: Al-Suddi gives the alternative sense: ask Me, and I will give you what you ask for.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r1.anchor: وجوز أن يكون المعنى اسألوني أعطكم وهو المروي عن السدي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r2.claim: On the asking interpretation, being arrogant toward worship means being arrogant toward supplication, which is worship and one of its best forms.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r2.anchor: يستكبرون عن دعائي لأن الدعاء من العبادة ومن أفضل أنواعها

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas said the best worship is supplication and recited this verse; al-Hakim authenticated the report, transmitted by Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Hakim.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r3.anchor: بل روي ابن المنذر والحاكم وصححه عن ابن عباس أنه قال : أفضل العبادة الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r4.claim: The threat addresses arrogance toward supplication, a habit of the affluent and extravagant; believers instead turn humbly to God through all their changing circumstances.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r4.anchor: والتوعد على الاستكبار عنه لأن ذلك عادة المترفين المسرفين وإنما المؤمن يتضرع إلى الله تعالى في كل تقلباته

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r5.claim: Attaching the object of arrogance to worship signals that supplication is a form of humility: worship entails submission, and asking God cannot itself be arrogance.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r5.anchor: وفي إيقاع العبادة صلة الاستكبار ما يؤذن بأن الدعاء باب من أبواب الخضوع لأن العبادة خضوع

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r6.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashf finds the asking interpretation clearer and more contextual: the surah contrasts disputing God's signs in arrogance with supplicating and submitting to them in humility.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r6.anchor: قال في الكشف : وهذا الوجه أظهر بحسب اللفظ وأنسب إلى السياق

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r7.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r7.claim: Al-Kashf reads the conjunction as linking one complete narrative to another with the same purpose; the later passage at 40:69 makes explicit the surah's theme of refuting disputants, while its ending echoes the opening warning at 40:4.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r7.anchor: والعطف في قوله تعالى : ( وقال ) من عطف مجموع قصة على مجموع أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi agrees that the asking interpretation is clearer in wording: the worship interpretation requires two figurative moves, while the asking reading requires only one for My worship, or none if the possessive refers back to the prior mention; he is less convinced by the contextual argument.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r8.anchor: وما ذكره من أظهرية هذا الوجه بحسب اللفظ ظاهر جدا لما في الأولى من ارتكاب خلاف الظاهر قبل الحاجة إليه في موضعين

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r9.claim: Astajib is jussive as the answer to an imperative: if you call on Me, I answer you.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r9.anchor: وأيا ما كان ( فأستجب ) جزم في جواب الأمر

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r10.claim: On either interpretation, answering is conditional on God's will according to Al-Alusi's theological principles, as stated explicitly in 6:41.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r10.anchor: والاستجابة على الوجهين مشروطة بالمشيئة حسبما تقتضيه أصولنا وقد صرح بذلك في استجابة الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r11.claim: Arrogance toward worship, whether supplication or another form of worship, is unbelief and entails the threat stated in the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p81#2/r11.anchor: والاستكبار عن عبادة الله تعالى دعاء كانت أو غيره كفر يترتب عليه ما ذكر في الآية الكريمة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r1.claim: Refraining from supplication without arrogance can be blameworthy or appropriate, depending on the circumstance.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r1.anchor: وأما ترك ذلك لا عن استكبار فتفصيل الكلام فيه لا يخفى والمقامات في ترك الدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r2.claim: A Prophetic report from Abu Hurayra says that whoever does not supplicate to God incurs His anger; Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shayba, and al-Hakim transmit it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r2.anchor: من لم يدع الله تعالى يغضب عليه أخرجه أحمد وابن أبي شيبة والحاكم عن أبي هريرة مرفوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r3.claim: As a counterexample of appropriate restraint, Abraham reportedly left supplication when thrown into the fire, saying that God's knowledge of his state made asking unnecessary; Al-Alusi presents this tentatively.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r3.anchor: وقد يحسن كما يدل عليه ما روي من ترك الخليل عليه السلام الدعاء يوم ألقي في النار وقوله علمه بحالي يغني عن سؤالي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr, Zayd b. Ali, and Abu Ja'far read the verb in the passive, meaning they will be admitted; transmissions differ from Asim and Abu Amr.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p82/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو بكر وزيد بن علي وأبو جعفر ( سيدخلون )

TIRMIDHI:3247/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3247/r1.speaker: النبي
TIRMIDHI:3247/r1.claim: Al-Nuʿman b. Bashir reports that the Prophet called supplication worship and then recited the verse; Tirmidhi grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
TIRMIDHI:3247/r1.anchor: النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقُولُ ‏"‏ الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ

TIRMIDHI:3372/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3372/r1.speaker: النبي
TIRMIDHI:3372/r1.claim: Al-Nuʿman b. Bashir reports that the Prophet called supplication worship and recited the verse; Tirmidhi grades it ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ, says it is known only through Dharr, whom he calls trustworthy.
TIRMIDHI:3372/r1.anchor: عَنِ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ ‏"‏ الدُّعَاءُ هُوَ الْعِبَادَةُ

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r3.claim: The command to call on God means worship Him alone; He answers by rewarding and forgiving, with acceptance expressed as a response.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r3.anchor: {وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم} أي: اعبدوني دون غيري أجبكم وأثبكم وأغفر لكم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r4.claim: The Prophet says that supplication itself is worship, then recites this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r4.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول على المنبر: "إن الدعاء هو العبادة" ثم قرأ:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r5.claim: The Prophet says that whoever does not supplicate to God incurs God's anger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r5.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من لم يدع الله غضب الله عليه"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r6.claim: Another view defines supplication as remembrance and asking.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وأبو بكر والآخرون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Jaafar, and Abu Bakr read the passive form yudkhalun; other readers use the active yadkhulun. Dakhir means humbled and abject.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p156/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير 111/ب وأبو جعفر وأبو بكر: "سيدخلون" بضم الياء وفتح الخاء، وقرأ الآخرون بفتح الياء وضم الخاء

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r3.claim: “Call upon Me” means worship Me; alternatively petition, with refusal to ask treated as refusal to worship, or prayer as a form of worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r3.anchor: وقال ربكم ادعونى } اعبدوني. { أستجب لكم } أثبكم

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r4.claim: God’s response to the call means that He rewards the worshipper.

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r5.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو بكر
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū Bakr read with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on khāʾ, the passive.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:59-61/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو بكر «سيدخلون» بضم الياء وفتح الخاء.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r14.claim: “Call on Me” means respond to God by worshiping Him alone and asking for promised victory; worshipful submission by supplication, prayer, or otherwise counts as supplication.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r14.anchor: استجيبوا لي بأن تعبدوني وحدي فتسألوني ما وعدتكم به من النصرة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r15.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r15.claim: The Prophet’s saying “supplication is worship” supports Biqāʿī’s broad reading of supplication as encompassing worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r15.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( الدعاء هو العبادة )

BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as “affirm My oneness, and I will forgive you.”
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r16.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : وحدوني اغفر لكم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r17.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r17.speaker: الثوري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r17.claim: When al-Thawrī was asked to supplicate, he replied that abandoning sins is itself supplication.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r17.anchor: وعن الثوري أنه قيل له : ادع

BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r18.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r18.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r18.claim: God may answer by granting the requested thing in this world, removing a comparable harm, or reserving the reward for the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r18.anchor: في الدنيا أي بإيجاد ما دعوتم به

BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r19.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r19.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r19.claim: This promise parallels God’s assurance that He answers the caller who calls upon Him in al-Baqara 2:186.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r20.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r20.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r20.claim: People must not rely on the promise and abandon supplication, since supplication is the core of worship and each person is enabled for what they were created to do.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r20.anchor: ولا تتكلوا على ما سبق به الوعد فتتركوا الدعاء

BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r21.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r21.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r21.claim: Al-Qushayrī is cited for the saying that supplication is the key to response and lawful food its teeth.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p528/r21.anchor: قال القشيري , وقيل : الدعاء مفتاح الإجابة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r1.claim: Pride is a usual cause of abandoning supplication, so the threat warns against refusing the call to worship while implicitly encouraging prayer.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r1.anchor: ولما كان السبب في ترك الدعاء في العادة الكبر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r2.claim: Being too proud for worship means refusing God’s call, disputing His signs, and turning away from calling upon Him in hardship and ease.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r2.anchor: عن الاستجابة لي فيما دعوت من العبادة بالمجادلة في آياتي

BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r3.claim: They enter Hell under a certain promise, humbled and abased as fitting recompense for their pride.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r4.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by cross-reference: mentioning supplication first implies its omission later, while worship mentioned later implies its omission at first.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p529/r4.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الدعاء أولا دليلا على حذفه ثانيا

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the Dajjāl remains forty mornings and reaches every watering place; days are successively like a Friday, a month, and a year.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: يخرج الدجال فيمكث في الأرض أربعين صباحا يبلغ منها كل منهل

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r2.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r2.claim: ʿUbayd reports the Prophet saying people who accompany the lying Dajjāl for food and grazing share God's wrath.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r2.anchor: عن عبيد بن عمير رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: ليصحبن الدجال قوم يقولون

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r3.speaker: أشعث بن أبي الشعثاء
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r3.claim: Ashʿath's father recounts Ibn Masʿūd's warning not to talk much of the Dajjāl, since a heavenly decree may descend faster than rumors spread.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r3.anchor: عن أشعث بن أبي الشعثاء عن أبيه قال: ذكر الدجال عند عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه فقال: لا تكثروا ذكره

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r4.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r4.claim: Al-Nuʿmān reports the Prophet calling supplication worship, glossing worship as devotion to God alone, and reciting this verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r4.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: الدعاء تلو العبادة ثم قرأ

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r5.claim: In al-Nuʿmān's report, the Prophet glosses God's worship as supplication.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r5.anchor: قال: عن دعائي {سيدخلون جهنم داخرين} هل تدرون ما عبادة الله

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r6.speaker: البراء
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r6.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports the Prophet saying supplication itself is worship and reciting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r6.anchor: عن البراء رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: إن الدعاء هو العبادة وقرأ

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses calling upon God as worshipping Him.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {ادعوني أستجب لكم} قال: اعبدوني

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r8.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r8.claim: Al-Suddī glosses entering Hell humbled as entering it abased.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r8.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في قوله {سيدخلون جهنم داخرين} قال: صاغرين

DURR-FULL:v7p300/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r9.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r9.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet glossing supplication as seeking forgiveness.
DURR-FULL:v7p300/r9.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: الدعاء الإستغفار

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r1.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying whoever does not supplicate to God incurs God's anger.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r1.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: من لم يدع الله يغضب عليه

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r2.speaker: معاذ
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r2.claim: Muʿādh says supplication benefits against calamities already come and not yet come, so believers should invoke God.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r2.anchor: عن معاذ رضي الله عنه قال: لن ينفع حذر من قدر ولكن الدعاء ينفع مما نزل ومما لم ينزل

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r3.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying that when God opens supplication for a servant, the servant should pray because God answers.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r3.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إذا فتح الله على عبد بالدعاء فليدع

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r4.speaker: أنس بن مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r4.claim: Anas reports the Prophet saying God loves persistent supplicants.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r4.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: إن الله يحب الملحين في الدعاء

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r5.speaker: وهب بن منبه
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r5.claim: Wahb cites a divine saying that God sends affliction to elicit supplication.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r5.anchor: عن وهب بن منبه رضي الله عنه قال: نجد فيما أنزل الله تعالى في بعض الكتب أن الله تعالى يقول: أنزل البلاء

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r6.claim: Anas transmits God's promise to forgive the servant who calls and hopes, even if sins fill earth or reach heaven, when he seeks forgiveness.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r6.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه في قوله {ادعوني أستجب لكم} قال: قال ربكم: عبدي إنك ما دعوتني ورجوتني

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās calls supplication the best worship and cites this verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما قال: أفضل العبادة الدعاء وقرأ {وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم}

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r8.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r8.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the promise means act and rejoice: God answers believers doing good and increases them from His bounty.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r8.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه في قوله {ادعوني أستجب لكم} قال: اعملوا وابشروا فإنه حق على الله

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r9.speaker: كعب
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r9.claim: Kaʿb says this community received a gift denied other communities: the chosen person is told to ask and be given.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r9.anchor: عن كعب رضي الله عنه أنه تلا هذه الآية فقال: ما أعطي أحد من الأمم ما أعطيت هذه الأمة

DURR-FULL:v7p301/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r10.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r10.claim: Asked which worship is best, the Prophet answers that a person supplicate for himself.
DURR-FULL:v7p301/r10.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي العبادة أفضل فقال: دعاء المرء لنفسه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3268#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3268#3/r1.speaker: كعب الأحبار
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3268#3/r1.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar says this community received three privileges denied earlier communities except their prophets: the community witnesses over people, its law imposes no hardship, and it is told to call on God and He will answer.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3268#3/r1.anchor: قال كعب الاحبار : اعطيت هذه الامة ثلاثا لم تعطهن امة قبلهم الا نبي

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3268#3/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3268#3/r2.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3268#3/r2.claim: The Prophet says supplication is worship, then recites the command to call on God and its warning against those who arrogantly refuse His worship.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3268#3/r2.anchor: عن ذر ، عن يسيع الكندي ، عن النعمان بن بشير رضي الله ، عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' ان الدعاء هو العبادة ' ثم قرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r1.claim: The conjunction before lakin is a verbal embellishment: the sentence could stand separately, but lakin often follows a coordinating waw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r1.anchor: يكثر أن تقع بعد واو العطف لكانت الجملة جديرة بالفصل دون عطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r2.claim: The ‘most people’ are the polytheists, who greatly outnumbered the believers at the time.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r2.anchor: هم المشركون ، وهم يومئذ أكثر من المؤمنين جدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r3.claim: Disputes over God’s signs concern both divine oneness and resurrection: the later exchange about partners illustrates the first, while the account of chains and punishment illustrates the second. The creation argument supports resurrection before the call to pray warns against idolatry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r3.anchor: تشمل مجادلتهم في وحدانية الإلهية كما دل عليه قوله الآتي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r4.claim: The command returns to the earlier call for exclusive prayer, which followed rebuke of the polytheists and a reminder that only the one who turns to God reflects; after intervening warnings, it embraces believers’ pure worship and connects to the failed prayer of disbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r4.anchor: عاد الكلام الآن إلى ما يشمل عبادة المؤمنين الخالصة لله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r5.claim: Because prayer earlier meant both worship and asking for a need, this command gathers both senses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r5.anchor: معنى العبادة ، ومعنى سؤال المطلوب ، أردف بهذا الأمر الجامع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r6.claim: ‘Your Lord said’ may refer to God’s inward speech, His will regarding what He would say when willing creation into being.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r6.anchor: ما تعلقت إرادة الله تعلقا صلاحيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r7.claim: Alternatively, it may be literal speech in earlier-revealed verses, such as the command to call on God sincerely; the verse about answering a caller in al-Baqara came later.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r7.anchor: إخبارا عن أقوال مضت في آيات قبل نزول هذه الآية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p180/r8.claim: A third possibility is that the past tense is figurative for the present: ‘Your Lord says: Call on Me.’

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r1.claim: Al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir reports the Prophet saying ‘supplication is worship,’ then reciting this verse; al-Tirmidhi grades the hadith hasan sahih.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r1.anchor: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r2.claim: Du‘a can mean calling, which acknowledges the one called, or requesting; asking God for a need is its common literal meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r2.anchor: بمعنى النداء المستلزم للاعتراف بالمنادى ، ويطلق على الطلب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r3.claim: Du‘a can also stand figuratively for worship because worship involves calling the one worshipped with reverence and supplication; this usage is less common. Quranic ‘worship’ means singling God out and acknowledging His oneness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r3.anchor: على عبادة الله على طريق الكناية لأن العبادة لا تخلو من دعاء المعبود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r4.claim: Istijaba commonly means granting a request; it can also mean accepting worship by forgiving prior shirk and rewarding acts of faith.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r4.anchor: والاستجابة تطلق على إعطاء المسؤول لمن سأله وهو أشهر إطلاقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r5.claim: If the command means asking for needs, the response depends on God’s will or fulfillment of the request’s conditions; He may grant the request, something better in this life, or its recompense in the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r5.anchor: ترتب الاستجابة على ذلك الطلب معلقا على مشيئة الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r6.claim: If the command means exclusive worship, God’s response is acceptance of repentance from shirk, which is assured.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r7.claim: The pairing of the two terms, followed by the reference to worship, signals an ellipsis-like combination: du‘a means both asking and worship, while response means answering and accepting worship’s effects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r7.anchor: علمنا أن في المعنى المراد ما يشبه الاحتباك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r8.claim: Ud‘uni is used for both meanings through the full scope of a shared homonym.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p181/r8.anchor: مستعمل في معنييه بطريقة عموم المشترك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r1.claim: Astajib is used both literally and figuratively; the context supplies the cue, making the expression concise and comprehensive.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r2.claim: Calling God ‘your Lord’ hints that the addressees owe obedience to His command; this wording does not invoke His favors or describe His attributes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r2.anchor: في هذا الوصف وإضافته من الإيماء إلى وجوب امتثال أمره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r3.claim: The warning about hell explains the command by cautioning against refusing God’s call while turning to idols; God does not want His servants led to punishment, and the verse supports asking Him for needs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r3.anchor: تعليلا يفيد التحذير من إباية دعاء الله حين الإقبال على دعاء الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r4.claim: Polytheists prayed to God only when they did not expect their partners to answer, as in the verse about reaching land safely and turning away.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r4.anchor: وكان المشركون لا يضرعون إلى الله إلا إذا لم يتوسموا استجابة شركائهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r5.claim: Muslims agree that supplication is legitimate; they disagree with the Mu‘tazilites over whether it can repel a decree. This verse does not settle that dispute because they interpret ‘I will respond’ differently.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r5.anchor: ومشروعية الدعاء لا خلاف فيها بين المسلمين وإنما الخلاف في أنه ينفع في رد القدر أو لا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r6.claim: The verse about God being near when His servants call precedes this discussion in al-Baqara.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r7.claim: The relative pronoun introduces a clause that hints at the reason for the command.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r7.anchor: وفي الإتيان بالموصول إيماء إلى التعليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r8.claim: Dakhirin is a circumstantial accusative from the subject of ‘they will enter’; it means humbled or abased, and the verb dakhira has forms like both mana‘a and fariha.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r8.anchor: و { داخرين } حال من ضمير { سيدخلون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r9.claim: The majority read sayadkhulun in the active voice, with an open ya and a damma on kha.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r10.claim: Abu Ja‘far and Ruways from Ya‘qub read yudkhalun in the passive voice, with a damma on ya and a fatha on kha, meaning the angels of punishment will admit them to hell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p182/r10.anchor: وقرأه أبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r1.claim: Allah may be parsed as appositive to “your Lord”: the shift names the one owed obedience both by lordship and by divine perfection; the relative clause signals attributes and grounds worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون اسم الجلالة بدلا من

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r2.claim: Other parses make Allah the subject, with the relative clause adjectival and “that is Allah, your Lord” as predicate, or make the relative clause itself the predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون اسم الجلالة مبتدأ والموصول صفة له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r3.claim: He prefers treating the sentence as a fresh explanatory statement over apposition, since it better exposes their ingratitude, suits the argument’s proofs, and leads into the description of God as creator.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r3.anchor: واعتبار الجملة مستأنفة أحسن من اعتبار اسم الجلالة بدلا لأنه أنسب بالتوقيف على سوء شكرهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r4.claim: On the preferred reading, the punishment for arrogance follows because the offenders disbelieved God’s blessing in making night and day for them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p183/r4.anchor: أي تسببوا لأنفسهم بذلك العقاب لأنهم كفروا نعمة الله إذ جعل لهم الليل والنهار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r1.claim: The command to pray is a favor, blessing, and promise to Muḥammad's community, conditioned by God's will rather than a guaranteed response to every supplicant, especially one who oversteps in prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم آية تفضل ونعمة ووعد لأمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بالإجابة عند الدعاء، وهذا الوعد مقيد بشرط المشيئة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r2.claim: The Prophet criticized a supplicant who asked for the white palace to the right of Paradise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r2.anchor: لا سيما لمن تعدى في دعائه، فقد عاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم دعاء الذي قال: اللهم أعطني القصر الأبيض الذي عن يمين الجنة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r3.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r3.claim: A group interprets the promise as response through reward and victory, supported by the following reference to those who disdain worship.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة: معنى: ادعوني وأستجب، معناه: بالثواب والنصر، ويدل على هذا التأويل قوله: إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r4.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r4.claim: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr reports that the Prophet called supplication worship and recited this verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r4.anchor: ويحتج له لحديث النعمان بن بشير أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الدعاء هو العبادة» وقرأ هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the command as affirming God's oneness so that He will forgive.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المعنى: وحدوني أغفر لكم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r6.speaker: الثوري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r6.claim: When al-Thawrī was asked to pray to God, he replied that abandoning sins is prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r6.anchor: وقيل للثوري: ادع الله، فقال: إن ترك الذنوب هو الدعاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r7.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū Jaʿfar read sayudkhalūn with passive ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on khāʾ; Nāfiʿ, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, Ibn ʿĀmir, al-Ḥasan, and Shayba read the active form; Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim vary.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p566/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو جعفر: «سيدخلون» بضم الياء وفتح الخاء. وقرأ نافع وحمزة والكسائي وابن عامر والحسن وشيبة: بفتح الياء وضم الخاء، واختلف عن أبي عمرو وعن عاصم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the command as “affirm My oneness and worship Me,” with a promise of reward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r1.anchor: أحدهما وحدوني واعبدوني أثبكم قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r2.claim: Al-Suddi interprets it as “ask Me, and I will give to you.”

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r3.claim: Two interpretations are given for those who disdain worship: disdain for God's oneness, or for supplication and asking.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r3.anchor: فيه قولان أحدهما عن توحيدي والثاني عن دعائي ومسألتي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو بكر عن عاصم وعباس بن الفضل عن أبي عمرو
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Bakr from Asim, and Abbas ibn al-Fadl from Abu Amr read the verb with ḍamma on its yāʾ; the other readers use fatḥa.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p234/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو بكر عن عاصم وعباس بن الفضل عن أبي عمرو سيدخلون بضم الياء

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r1.claim: God addresses people; calling on Him means affirming His oneness and worshipping Him.

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r2.claim: I will answer you means I will reward you, as the following warning about those arrogant toward worship indicates.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r2.anchor: {أستجب لكم} ؛ أي : أثبكم بقرينة قوله تعالى : {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي}

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r3.claim: Those who are arrogant toward worship disdain obedience and will enter Hell humiliated and abased.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r3.anchor: {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي} يتعظمون عن طاعتي {سيدخلون جهنم} حال كونهم {داخرين} ؛ أي : صاغرين أذلاء

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r4.claim: Dākhirīn means lowly and humiliated; the commentary also gives the Persian gloss and Arabic root sense of becoming small and abased.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r4.anchor: {داخرين} ؛ أي : صاغرين أذلاء فإن الدخو بالفارسية : (خوارشدن.

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r5.claim: If the command means asking, refraining from asking is treated as arrogance toward worship, with the second phrase replacing the first for emphasis.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r5.anchor: وإن فسر بالسؤال كان الاستكبار الصارف عنه منزلا منزلة الاستكبار عن العبادة ، فأقيم الثاني مقام الأول للمبالغة.

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, worship here means supplication, a particular instance expressed by the general term through figurative usage.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r6.anchor: أو المراد بالعبادة الدعاء ، فإنه من أفضل أبوابها ، فأطلق العام على الخاص مجازا.

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r7.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r7.claim: Al-Kāshifī exhorts people to ask, since God's treasury is abundant and His generosity meets the needs of those who bring their requests.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r7.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (مرد از دعا سؤالست يعني بخواهيد كه خزانة من مالا مالست وكرم من بخشدة آمال

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r8.claim: Adab of prayer calls for attentiveness, frankness, and accuracy; the corresponding divine answers are promptness, fulfillment, and giving.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r8.anchor: يقال : ادعوني بلا غفلة أستجب لكم بلا مهلة ادعوني بلا خفاء أستجب لكم بالوفاء ادعوني بلا خطأ ، أستجب لكم بالعطاء

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r9.speaker: قيل
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r9.claim: Prayer requires eating lawful food; another saying calls prayer the key to need and a lawful morsel its teeth.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r9.anchor: ادعوني بشرط الدعاء ، وهو الأكل من الحلال. قيل : الدعاء مفتاح الحاجة وأسنانه لقمة الحلال.

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r10.speaker: الحكيم الترمذي
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r10.claim: Al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī warns that prayer without prior repentance, turning to God, lawful food, following the Sunna, and guarding the inner secret is rejected, perhaps answered with rejection and curse.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r10.anchor: قال الحكيم الترمذي قدس سره : من دعا الله ، ولم يعمر قبل ذلك سبيل الدعاء بالتوبة والإنابة وأكل الحلال واتباع السنن

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r11.speaker: ويقال
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r11.claim: God answers a supplicant either with the thing requested or with something better for them.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r11.anchor: يقال : كان من دعاه استجاب له إما بما سأله

BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r12.claim: The commentary says polytheists do not truly call on God, deniers posit a deity without divine attributes, and anthropomorphists posit bodily parts; God has no likeness and is all-hearing, all-seeing.
BURSEVI:v8p152#2/r12.anchor: لأنهم إنما يعبدون إلها لا صفات له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r1.claim: Inviting servants to supplicate and guaranteeing an answer is an expression of God’s favor and generosity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r1.anchor: هذا من فضله، تبارك وتعالى، وكرمه أنه ندب عباده إلى دعائه، وتكفل لهم بالإجابة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r2.speaker: سفيان الثوري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r2.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri says God loves servants who ask Him frequently and dislikes those who do not ask, unlike other beings; Ibn Abi Hatim transmits his saying.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r2.anchor: كما كان سفيان الثوري يقول: يا من أحب عباده إليه من سأله فأكثر سؤاله،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r3.speaker: الشاعر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r3.claim: An unnamed poet illustrates the point: God is displeased when people leave off asking Him, while human beings grow displeased when asked.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r3.anchor: الله يغضب إن تركت سؤاله … وبني آدم حين يسأل يغضب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r4.speaker: كعب الأحبار
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r4.claim: Ka'b al-Ahbar, narrated by Qatada, lists three privileges of this community: it witnesses over humanity, faces no religious hardship as in 22:78, and is told to call on God for a response as prophets were.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r4.anchor: قال كعب الأحبار: أعطيت هذه الأمة ثلاثا لم تعطهن (3) أمة قبلهم إلا نبي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r5.claim: In a report from his Lord, the Prophet lists four matters: worship God alone, God’s reward for good, human supplication met by divine response, and wishing other people what one wishes oneself; Abu Ya'la transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r5.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك، رضي الله عنه، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم -فيما يروي عن ربه عز وجل-قال:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r6.claim: The Prophet says supplication is worship and recites 40:60; Ahmad and the Sunan compilers transmit it, and al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p153/r6.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الدعاء هو العبادة"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r1.claim: The hadith that supplication is worship is also transmitted by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Jarir through Shu'ba and Mansur, and by Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim; al-Hakim calls its chain sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r1.anchor: ورواه أبو داود، والترمذي، والنسائي، وابن جرير أيضا، من حديث شعبة، عن منصور

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r2.claim: The Prophet says whoever does not call on God incurs His anger; Ahmad alone transmits this version, and Ibn Kathir says its chain is acceptable.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة [رضي الله عنه] (6) قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من لم يدع الله، عز وجل، غضب عليه"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r3.claim: Another Ahmad narration says the one who does not ask God angers Him; Ibn Ma'in identifies Abu al-Malih as Subayh, and Abu Salih as al-Khuzi, also called al-Farisi in al-Bazzar’s version.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r3.anchor: حدثنا صبيح أبو المليح: سمعت أبا صالح يحدث عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "من لا يسأله يغضب عليه"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r4.claim: A note found on Muhammad ibn Maslama’s sword after his death says the Prophet described divine opportunities in the remaining days; one timely supplication may meet mercy and bring its owner lasting success.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p154/r4.anchor: لما مات محمد بن مسلمة الأنصاري، وجدنا في ذؤابة (15) سيفه كتابا: "بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم، سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r1.claim: Arrogance toward God’s worship means refusing to call on Him and affirm His oneness; such people enter Hell humbled and abased.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r1.anchor: أي: عن دعائي وتوحيدي، {سيدخلون جهنم داخرين} أي: صاغرين حقيرين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r2.claim: The Prophet says the arrogant will be raised on Judgment Day as tiny beings in human form, covered in humiliation, then confined in Hell’s prison Bulas, covered by fire and made to drink the foul fluid of Hell’s inhabitants.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r2.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يحشر المتكبرون يوم القيامة أمثال الذر، في صور الناس، يعلوهم كل شيء من الصغار

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r3.speaker: رجل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r3.claim: A man heard a voice in Byzantine lands marvel that someone who knows God would ask anyone else for needs or risk God’s anger to please another; the speaker identified himself as human and urged attention to what matters.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p155/r3.anchor: حدثني رجل قال: كنت أسير ذات يوم في أرض الروم، فسمعت هاتفا من فوق رأس جبل وهو يقول:

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r1.claim: Here call on Me means worship Me; the following clause confirms this, and the Qur’an often uses supplication for worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r1.anchor: والدعاء بمعنى العبادة كثير في القرآن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r2.claim: Here response means reward; Mujāhid glosses the verse worship Me, I will reward you.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r3.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says to act and rejoice, since God is bound to answer believers who do good and increase them from His bounty.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r3.anchor: وعن الحسن وقد سئل عنها : اعملوا وأبشروا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r4.speaker: الثوري
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r4.claim: When al-Thawrī was asked to pray, he replied that abandoning sins is prayer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r4.anchor: وعن الثوري أنه قيل له : ادع الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says that if obedience to God occupies a servant instead of supplication, God gives him something better than what He gives those who ask.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r5.anchor: إذا شغل عبدي طاعتي عن الدعاء ، أعطيته أفضل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r6.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r6.claim: Al-Nuʿmān b. Bashīr reports that the Prophet called supplication worship and recited this verse.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r6.anchor: وروى النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنه ، عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r7.claim: Alternatively, the verse can mean supplicate to Me and I will answer; worship here means supplication, one of worship’s best avenues.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يريد الدعاء والاستجابة على ظاهرهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says supplication is the best worship.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r8.anchor: قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أفضل العبادة الدعاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r9.speaker: كعب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r9.claim: Kaʿb says this community received three privileges given only to a sent prophet: witness over people (2:143), freedom from religious hardship (5:6), and the promise that prayer will be answered.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r9.anchor: وعن كعب : أعطى الله هذه الأمة ثلاث خلال

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the command as affirm My oneness and I will forgive you, explaining supplication as worship and worship as monotheism.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r10.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : وحدوني أغفر لكن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p179#3/r11.claim: The phrase threatens those who arrogantly reject worship with entering Hell in abasement; dākhirīn means humbled.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as affirming God's lordship, for which He forgives sins.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r1.anchor: معناه وحدوني بالربوبية أغفر لكم ذنوبكم ، قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.claim: Jarir ibn Abd Allah says it means worship Me; God answers their worship.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r2.anchor: قاله جرير بن عبد الله ، أي اتبعكم على عبادتكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says ask Me and I will give to you.

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.claim: God answers a sincere supplicant, subject to divine wisdom.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r4.anchor: وإجابة الداعي عند صدق الرغبة مقيد بشرط الحكمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.speaker: قتادة عن كعب
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.claim: Qatada transmits Ka'b's three privileges: the community witnesses over peoples, faces no religious hardship, and receives answered prayer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p162#2/r5.anchor: وحكى قتادة أن كعب قال : أعطيت هذه الأمة ثلاثا لم تعطهن أمة قبلكم إلا نبي

MUQATIL:40:58-61/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:40:58-61/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:40:58-61/r4.claim: The command to call upon God is addressed to the people of Yemen.
MUQATIL:40:58-61/r4.anchor: وقال ربكم } لأهل اليمن: { ادعوني أستجب لكم } ، ثم ذكر كفار مكة

MUQATIL:40:58-61/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:40:58-61/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:40:58-61/r5.claim: Being arrogant toward God’s worship means being arrogant toward monotheism; Meccan unbelievers will enter Hell humbled.
MUQATIL:40:58-61/r5.anchor: يستكبرون عن عبادتي } يعنى عن التوحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r1.claim: Here call upon Me means worship Me, and I will reward you; the Qur'an often uses supplication for worship, as the following clause confirms.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ وقال ربكم ادعوني ﴾ اعبدوني ﴿ أستجب لكم ﴾ اثبكم فالدعاء بمعنى العباده كثير في القرآن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r2.claim: The Prophet said supplication is worship and recited this verse as proof.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r2.anchor: وقال عليه السلام الدعاء هو العبادة وقرا هذه الآية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it: affirm My oneness and I will forgive you, interpreting supplication as worship and worship as monotheism.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما وحدوني اغفر لكم وهذا تفسير للدعاء بالعبادة ثم للعبادة بالتوحيد

NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r4.claim: Another explanation is: ask Me and I will give to you.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r5.speaker: مكي وأبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r5.claim: Makkī and Abū ʿAmr read sayadkhulūn with the reading given in the commentary.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p78#5/r6.anchor: ﴿ سيدخلون جهنم ﴾ سيدخلون مكى وابو عمرو ﴿ داخرين ﴾

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r1.claim: Al-Nuʿmān ibn Bashīr reports that the Prophet called supplication worship and recited this verse; al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r1.anchor: روى النعمان بن بشير قال: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r2.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r2.claim: Most commentators likewise take the command to mean “affirm My oneness and worship Me”; God accepts their worship and forgives them.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r2.anchor: وكذا قال أكثر المفسرين وأن المعنى: وحدوني واعبدوني أتقبل عبادتكم وأغفر لكم

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes duʿāʾ here as remembrance, supplication and asking.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r4.claim: Anas reports the Prophet’s instruction to ask God for every need, even a sandal strap when it breaks.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r4.anchor: قال أنس: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r5.claim: A further explanation says duʿāʾ means leaving sins.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r6.speaker: كعب الأحبار
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r6.claim: Kaʿb al-Aḥbār, as related by Qatāda, says this community received three gifts previously given only to prophets: being witnesses to humanity (2:143), no hardship in religion (22:78), and the direct command to call upon God for a response.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r6.anchor: وحكى قتادة أن كعب الأحبار قال: أعطيت هذه الأمة ثلاثا لم تعطهن أمة قبلهم إلا نبي

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r7.claim: Al-Qurṭubī remarks that a statement like Kaʿb’s is not normally said from personal opinion.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r7.anchor: قلت: مثل هذا لا يقال من جهة الرأي.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r8.claim: A report raised to the Prophet from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit repeats the three gifts: the Prophet’s invitation to pray for a response, relief from religious hardship, and the community’s role as witnesses; al-Tirmidhī al-Ḥakīm includes it in Nawādir al-uṣūl.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r8.anchor: وقد جاء مرفوعا رواه ليث عن شهر بن حوشب عن عبادة بن الصامت، قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r9.speaker: خالد الربعي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r9.claim: Khālid al-Rabʿī marvels that the community is commanded to pray and promised a response without a condition, unlike some other promises; the comparison continues in the next segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60/r9.anchor: وكان خالد الربعي يقول: عجيب لهذه الأمة قيل لها: «ادعوني أستجب لكم» أمرهم بالدعاء ووعدهم الاستجابة

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r1.speaker: خالد الربعي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r1.claim: Khālid al-Rabʿī contrasts conditional promises to believers who do good (2:25) and to those who call God sincerely (40:14) with the unconditioned wording of this verse; he also cites a promise to believers without a good-works clause (10:2).
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r1.anchor: وبشر الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات [البقرة: 25] فهاهنا شرط، وقوله: وبشر الذين آمنوا أن لهم قدم صدق [يونس: 2] فليس فيه شرط

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r2.claim: People used to turn to prophets with their needs and ask the prophets to make the request to God for them.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r2.anchor: وكانت الأمة تفزع إلى أنبيائها في حوائجها حتى تسأل الأنبياء لهم ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r3.claim: Some explain the verse through the distinction between unrestricted and qualified wording, as discussed earlier under al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r3.anchor: وقد قيل: إن هذا من باب المطلق والمقيد على ما تقدم في «البقرة» بيانه.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r4.claim: “I will answer you” may mean “if I will,” as in God’s statement that He will remove what they call for if He wills.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r5.claim: The response may come in a form other than the exact request, as in the report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī discussed under al-Baqara.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r5.anchor: وقد تكون الاستجابة في غير عين المطلوب على حديث أبي سعيد الخدري

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وابن محيصن ورويس عن يعقوب وعياش عن أبي عمرو وأبو بكر والمفضل عن عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r6.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ruways from Yaʿqūb, ʿAyyāsh from Abū ʿAmr, and Abū Bakr and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿĀṣim read sayudkhalūn passively.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن محيصن ورويس عن يعقوب وعياش عن أبي عمرو وأبو بكر والمفضل عن عاصم { سيدخلون }

QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r7.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:40:60-64/r7.claim: The remaining readers use the active form yadkhulūn.

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r1.claim: Because resurrection is certain and only obedience benefits people then, obedience is urgent; supplication and humble pleading are the noblest kinds, so God commands them here.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r1.anchor: وكان من المعلوم بالضرورة أن الإنسان لا ينتفع في يوم القيامة إلا بطاعة الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r2.claim: Some read “call upon Me” as prayer, others as worship because the next clause says “My worship” and Qur’anic usage can equate calling with worship.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r2.anchor: واختلف الناس في المراد بقوله { ادعوني }

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r3.claim: Against construing “call” as worship, Razi says supplication itself confesses servitude, need, and lowliness; abandoning it can reflect pride about displaying servitude.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r3.anchor: الدعاء هو اعتراف بالعبودية والذلة والمسكنة

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r4.claim: A reply to the worship reading is that one should not leave the apparent meaning unless there is separate evidence requiring that shift.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r4.anchor: بأن ترك الظاهرة لا يصار إليه إلا بدليل منفصل

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r5.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r5.claim: Al-Kaabi says the promise applies when the requested outcome is beneficial and wise; he then asks what prayer adds if God already does what is best.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r5.anchor: أجاب الكعبي عنه بأن قال : الدعاء إنما يصح على شرط

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r6.speaker: الكعبي
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r6.claim: Al-Kaabi replies that prayer draws a person into reliance on God, and that the same determinist objection applies whether an act is known to occur or not to occur.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r6.anchor: أجاب الكعبي عنه بأن قال : الدعاء إنما يصح على شرط

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r7.claim: Razi says a prayer is genuine only when the heart has no reliance on wealth, status, relatives, friends, or personal effort; tongue-only prayer relies on other means, while a heart wholly turned to God is answered.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r7.anchor: فكل من دعا الله وفي قلبه ذرة من الاعتماد على ماله وجاهه

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r8.claim: This account gives glad tidings: complete detachment from everything besides God comes near death, when a person knows nothing can help but divine favor, so prayer then should be accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r8.anchor: أن انقطاع القلب بالكلية عما سوى الله لا يحصل إلا عند القرب من الموت

RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r9.claim: Razi notes that his fuller discussion of supplication appeared earlier in Surat al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v27p70#2/r9.anchor: واعلم أن الكلام السمتقصى في الدعاء قد سبق ذكره في سورة البقرة

RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r1.anchor: أي صاغرين وهذا إحسان عظيم من الله تعالى حيث ذكر الوعيد الشديد على ترك الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r2.claim: The severe threat for abandoning supplication is itself a great kindness from God.
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r2.anchor: وهذا إحسان عظيم من الله تعالى حيث ذكر الوعيد الشديد على ترك الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r3.claim: The command connects to prior blessings: since God granted great favors before people asked, He can grant lesser requests after they ask.
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r3.anchor: إني أنعمت عليك قبل طلبك لهذه النعم الجليلة العظيمة

RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r4.claim: The command also follows proof of knowledge: supplication presupposes recognizing God, so the preceding passage supplies ten signs of His existence, power, and wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v27p71/r4.anchor: الاشتغال بالدعاء لا بد وأن يكون مسبوقا بحصول المعرفة

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r1.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r1.claim: Many understand “Call upon Me” as “Worship Me,” also supported by the following warning against arrogance about worship.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r1.anchor: Call upon Me, or “Supplicate unto Me,” is understood by many to mean, “Worship Me,” as when the Prophet said

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r2.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r2.claim: The Prophet says supplication is worship and recites this verse.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r2.anchor: as when the Prophet said, “Supplication is worship,” and then recited this verse

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r3.claim: Alternatively, the verse enjoins supplication to God, which itself implies worship; many Muslims follow the Prophet by supplicating after obligatory prayers.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r3.anchor: The verse can also be understood as an injunction to call upon God, which would itself imply worship

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r4.claim: God's promise to respond does not mean every supplication is answered in this life.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r4.anchor: I shall respond to you is a promise from God, but it is not understood to mean that all supplications will be answered in this life

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r5.speaker: Ibn ʿAjībah
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAjībah says God grants the believer's request either in this life or stores it for the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r5.anchor: Ibn ʿAjībah writes, “There is no believer who calls upon God and asks Him for something but that God gives it to him

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r6.claim: Supplication is meritorious because it humbly acknowledges servitude, abasement, poverty before God, and complete need of Him.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r6.anchor: Supplication is considered among the most meritorious of acts, because in humbly imploring God one admits to one’s servitude

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r7.claim: Most who fail to call upon God do so from pride and arrogance.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r7.anchor: Thus most who fail to call upon God do so out of pride and arrogance

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r8.speaker: ḥadīth qudsī
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r8.claim: A famous sacred report says that one whose remembrance distracts from supplication receives something more bountiful than what is given to those who supplicate.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r8.anchor: For one whose remembrance of Me has distracted him from imploring Me, I shall give him that which is more bountiful

STUDYQURAN:40:60/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r9.claim: The commentary points to its discussion of calling upon God at 2:186.
STUDYQURAN:40:60/r9.anchor: for more on the importance of “calling upon God,” see 2:186c

QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r4.claim: The promise to answer prayer is qualified by God's will, as another verse says He removes what people invoke Him to remove if He wills.

QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
