QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r5.claim: One view makes lawful food a condition of supplication, whose key is need and whose cause is a lawful morsel.

QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r6.speaker: غير مسمى
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r6.claim: One view says God answers everyone who calls, either with the requested thing or with something better.
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r6.anchor: ويقال كل من دعاه استجاب له إما بما يشاء له

QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r7.speaker: غير مسمى
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r7.claim: One view says an unbeliever does not truly invoke God because the unbeliever invokes a partner, while God has no partner.
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r7.anchor: الكافر ليس يدعوه ؛ لأنه إنما يدعو من له شريك

QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r8.speaker: غير مسمى
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r8.claim: If the address is to believers, they receive what they ask for in this life; God may defer it for the afterlife, making the servant wish it had all been deferred.
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r8.anchor: إذا ثبت أن هذا الخطاب للمؤمنين

QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r9.speaker: غير مسمى
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r9.claim: Spiritual readings pair prayer with obedience, freedom from heedlessness, repentance, effort, or asking, and pair the answer with reward, immediacy, grace, relief, or generosity.
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r9.anchor: ادعوني بالطاعات استجب لكم بالثواب والدرجات

QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r10.claim: Here worship means supplication: those who proudly refuse to call on God enter Hell humbled.
QUSHAYRI:v3p140/r10.anchor: أن يستكبرون عن دعائي ، سيدخلون جهنم صاغرين

TAB-FULL:v20p351/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r2.claim: “Call upon Me” means worship God and devote worship exclusively to Him instead of idols and other objects of worship.
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r2.anchor: ادعوني: يقول: اعبدوني وأخلصوا لي العبادة دون من تعبدون من دوني من الأوثان والأصنام وغير ذلك

TAB-FULL:v20p351/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r3.claim: God answers their prayer by pardoning and showing mercy.

TAB-FULL:v20p351/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the command as “affirm My oneness and I will forgive you.”
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ادعوني أستجب لكم} [غافر: 60] يقول: «وحدوني أغفر لكم»

TAB-FULL:v20p351/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r5.claim: The Prophet says that supplication is worship, then recites this verse.
TAB-FULL:v20p351/r5.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الدعاء هو العبادة» وقرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v20p354/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r1.claim: A report from al-Nuʿmān says the Prophet glossed “My worship” in this verse as “My supplication.”
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r1.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن عبادتي دعائي» ثم تلا هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v20p354/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r2.speaker: أنس
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r2.claim: Anas says supplication is not half of worship but all of it.
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r2.anchor: قلت لأنس: يا أبا حمزة أبلغك أن الدعاء نصف العبادة؟ قال: «لا بل هو العبادة كلها»

TAB-FULL:v20p354/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r3.claim: Al-Suddi transmits another report from al-Nuʿmān that the Prophet said supplication is worship and recited 40:60.
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r3.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الدعاء هو العبادة» ثم قرأ هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v20p354/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r4.speaker: سفيان
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r4.claim: Sufyan says leaving sins is itself supplication.
TAB-FULL:v20p354/r4.anchor: قيل لسفيان: ادع الله، قال: «إن ترك الذنوب هو الدعاء»

TAB-FULL:v20p354#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p354#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p354#2/r1.claim: The arrogant make themselves too great to worship God alone and affirm His divinity alone; they will enter Hell humiliated.
TAB-FULL:v20p354#2/r1.anchor: عبادتي} [غافر: 60] إن الذين يستكبرون عن دعائي

TAB-FULL:v20p354#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p354#2/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p354#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddi takes “My worship” here to mean “My supplication.”
TAB-FULL:v20p354#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي، {إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي} [غافر: 60] قال: «عن دعائي»

SULAMI:v2p212/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p212/r1.speaker: الوراق
SULAMI:v2p212/r1.claim: Al-Warraq says to invoke God from desperate need and refuge, as one with no shelter or destination besides Him, and He will answer.
SULAMI:v2p212/r1.anchor: قال الوراق : ادعوني على جدارة الاضطرار والالتجاء دعاء من لا يكون له ملجأ ولا مرجع إلى سواي : استجب

SULAMI:v2p212/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p212/r2.speaker: محمد بن علي
SULAMI:v2p212/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ali warns that prayer may be rejected if one has not prepared for it with repentance, lawful food, following the Sunna, and guarding the inner self.
SULAMI:v2p212/r2.anchor: وقال محمد بن علي : من دعا الله ولم يعمر قبل ذلك سبيل الدعاء بالتوبة والإنابة وأكل الحلال

SULAMI:v2p212/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p212/r3.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p212/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Mu'adh says sincere reliance in supplication brings an answer to sound prayer.
SULAMI:v2p212/r3.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : ادعوني بصدق الالتجاء استجب لكم صالح الدعاء .

SULAMI:v2p212/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p212/r4.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p212/r4.claim: Sahl says supplication is the best deed because it expresses poverty, need, refuge, and humble pleading.
SULAMI:v2p212/r4.anchor: وقيل لسهل : ما معنى قولهم : الدعاء افضل العمل ؟ فقال : لأن فيه الفقر والفاقة والالتجاء

SULAMI:v2p212/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p212/r5.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p212/r5.claim: Ibn Ata describes supplication as having pillars, wings, times, and causes: present and humble heart, sincerity, dawn, and blessings on Muhammad respectively.
SULAMI:v2p212/r5.anchor: قال ابن عطاء رحمة الله عليه : للدعاء أركان واجنحة وأسباب وأوقات فإن وافق اركانه قوى

SULAMI:v2p214#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r1.speaker: الشبلي
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r1.claim: Al-Shibli marvels at the divine command's mystery, then says inwardly that one must be without self in the secret of the unseen; outwardly, invoke God alone, for finding Him means finding everything.
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r1.anchor: سمعت الشبلي يقول : وقد سئل عن قوله : ﴿ ادعوني أستجب لكم ﴾ فقال : اوه من أمر ولمن أمر

SULAMI:v2p214#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r2.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r2.claim: Al-Nasrabadi says God deputized creatures to pray and deputized Himself to answer; each prays for the one who deputized him, while those not so deputized are deprived of prayer and response.
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r2.anchor: سمعت النصرآباذي يقول : ناب عن خلقه بالدعاء وناب عنهم بالاجابة فكل يدعو على ما ناب عنه

SULAMI:v2p214#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r3.claim: Ibn Ata reads the command as reciprocal: invoke Me and respond to Me, and I will answer you.
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ادعوني واستجيبوا استجب لكم .

SULAMI:v2p214#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r4.claim: Some people think they pray to God while in truth they invoke and worship someone else.
SULAMI:v2p214#3/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : كم منا دعا ربه عند نفسه وهو في الحقيقة دعا غيره وعبد سواه .

TUSTARI:40:60/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:40:60/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:40:60/r1.claim: A prayer made with marwa is certainly answered; every believer's prayer is answered either in the exact request, without the person knowing, by averting harm, or by recording a good deed.

TUSTARI:40:60/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:40:60/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:40:60/r2.claim: Supplication is called the best act because it is humble pleading and reliance that displays poverty and need.
TUSTARI:40:60/r2.anchor: لأنه تضرع والتجاء وإظهار الفقر والفاقة

TABATABAI:40:56-60/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:56-60/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:56-60/r8.claim: The verse reminds them of the Hour, then the next verse calls them to pray; this recalls the believer from Pharaoh’s family warning of the Hour and that only God calls people in this world and the next.
TABATABAI:40:56-60/r8.anchor: ذكرهم تعالى في هذه الآية بإتيان الساعة وفي الآية التالية بدعوة ربهم إياهم إلى دعائه وعبادته

TABATABAI:40:60/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:60/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:60/r1.claim: The terms calling, supplication, and response are used broadly here; the author directs readers to his fuller discussion of prayer and response at 2:186.

TABATABAI:40:60/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:60/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:60/r2.anchor: الدخور الذلة، وقد بدل الدعاء عبادة فدل على أن الدعاء عبادة

TABATABAI:40:60/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:60/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:60/r3.claim: Calling the act of supplication worship shows that supplication is itself worship.
TABATABAI:40:60/r3.anchor: وقد بدل الدعاء عبادة فدل على أن الدعاء عبادة

TABATABAI:40:60/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:60/r4.speaker: الصحيفة السجادية
TABATABAI:40:60/r4.claim: A prayer in al-Ṣaḥīfa al-Sajjādiyya addresses God: You named calling You worship, leaving it arrogance, and threatened those who leave it with entry into Hell in humiliation.

TABATABAI:40:60/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:60/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:40:60/r5.claim: In al-Kāfī, Abū ʿAbd Allāh says to pray and not claim the matter is already decided, because prayer is worship; he cites the warning about those who disdain worship and the promise to pray.
TABATABAI:40:60/r5.anchor: عن حماد بن عيسى عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول ادع ولا تقل قد فرغ من الأمر

TABATABAI:40:60/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:60/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:60/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī explains that the report’s worship argument supports its initial command to pray, while the promise to answer supports its warning not to say the matter is already decided; the Imam cites the verse’s end before its beginning.
TABATABAI:40:60/r6.anchor: ولذا قدم عليه السلام في بيانه ذيل الآية على صدرها

TABATABAI:40:60/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:60/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:40:60/r7.claim: A report from Abū ʿAbd Allāh says that whoever is given supplication receives response, gratitude receives increase, and trust receives sufficiency, citing 65:3, 14:7, and this verse.
TABATABAI:40:60/r7.anchor: عن معاوية بن عمار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال يا معاوية من أعطي ثلاثة لم يحرم ثلاثة من أعطي الدعاء أعطي الإجابة

TABATABAI:40:60/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:60/r8.speaker: موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:40:60/r8.claim: Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar reports that people told al-Ṣādiq their prayers went unanswered; al-Ṣādiq replied that they call upon one they do not know.
TABATABAI:40:60/r8.anchor: في التوحيد بإسناده إلى موسى بن جعفر عليه السلام قال قال قوم للصادق عليه السلام ندعوه فلا يستجاب لنا

AKHFASH:v2p503/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p503/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p503/r1.claim: He identifies أستجب’s initial alif as the أفعل prefix, distinct from hamzat al-wasl and analogous to imperfect يـ and تـ; it is pronounced in connected or isolated speech.
AKHFASH:v2p503/r1.anchor: فقوله {أستجب} إنما هو "أفعل" هذه الألف سوى الف الوصل.

TABRISI:40:60/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو بكر غير الشموني وسهل؛ والباقون
TABRISI:40:60/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn Kathīr, Abū Bakr except al-Shamūnī, and Sahl read passive ‘will be entered’; others read active ‘will enter.’
TABRISI:40:60/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن كثير وأبو بكر غير الشموني وسهل سيدخلون بضم الياء وفتح الخاء والباقون

TABRISI:40:60/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:60/r17.claim: God responds when beneficial; that condition must be stated or understood, otherwise answering a harmful request would be wrong.
TABRISI:40:60/r17.anchor: يعني إذا اقتضت المصلحة أجابتكم وكل من يسأل الله شيئا ويدعوه فلا بد أن يشترط المصلحة

TABRISI:40:60#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:40:60#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets ‘call upon Me’ as affirming God’s oneness and worshipping Him, promising reward.
TABRISI:40:60#2/r1.anchor: وقيل: معناه وحدوني واعبدوني أثبكم عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:40:60#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:60#2/r2.claim: The Prophet’s saying ‘supplication is worship’ supports this reading; calling worship supplication makes its reward ‘response,’ matching the wording.
TABRISI:40:60#2/r2.anchor: ولما عبر عن العبادة بالدعاء جعل الإثابة استجابة ليتجانس اللفظ

TABRISI:40:60#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:60#2/r3.claim: The worship from which they are arrogant is supplication; they enter Hell abject and humiliated.
TABRISI:40:60#2/r3.anchor: { إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي } ودعائي { سيدخلون جهنم داخرين } أي صاغرين ذليلين

TABRISI:40:60#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:60#2/r4.claim: The verse shows supplication’s great rank and merit of turning to God alone.
TABRISI:40:60#2/r4.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على عظم قدر الدعاء عند الله تعالى وعلى فضل الانقطاع إليه

TABRISI:40:60#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60#2/r5.speaker: معاوية بن عمار
TABRISI:40:60#2/r5.claim: Muʿāwiya ibn ʿAmmār asked whether more prayer or supplication was better; after saying both were good, Abū ʿAbd Allāh chose more supplication, citing the verse and calling it the greatest worship.
TABRISI:40:60#2/r5.anchor: وقد روى معاوية بن عمار قال قلت لأبي عبد الله ع جعلني الله فداك ما تقول في رجلين دخلا المسجد جميعا

TABRISI:40:60#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60#2/r6.speaker: زرارة عن أبي جعفر
TABRISI:40:60#2/r6.claim: Zurāra reports from Abū Jaʿfar that this means supplication and supplication is the best worship.
TABRISI:40:60#2/r6.anchor: وروى زرارة عن أبي جعفر ع في هذه الآية قال: هو الدعاء وأفضل العبادة الدعاء

TABRISI:40:60#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:60#2/r7.speaker: حنان بن سدير عن أبيه
TABRISI:40:60#2/r7.claim: Ḥanān ibn Sudayr reports from his father that nothing is dearer to God than asking Him for what He has, and none more hateful than the arrogant who refuse worship and asking.
TABRISI:40:60#2/r7.anchor: وروى حنان بن سدير عن أبيه. قال: قلت لأبي جعفر أي العبادة أفضل؟ قال:

THALABI:v8p280/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p280/r1.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v8p280/r1.claim: Some interpreters take udʿūnī to mean remembrance, supplication, and asking.
THALABI:v8p280/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هو الذكر والدعاء والسؤال.

THALABI:v8p280/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p280/r2.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v8p280/r2.claim: Anas reports the Prophet instructing people to ask God for every need, even a sandal strap when it breaks; no grading is given.
THALABI:v8p280/r2.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

THALABI:v8p280/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p280/r3.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v8p280/r3.claim: Most commentators interpret God's worship here as His oneness and obedience.
THALABI:v8p280/r3.anchor: إن الذين يستكبرون عن عبادتي توحيدي وطاعتي، عن أكثر المفسرين.

THALABI:v8p280/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p280/r4.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v8p280/r4.claim: Al-Suddi reads the phrase as referring to God's supplication.

THALABI:v8p280/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p280/r5.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
THALABI:v8p280/r5.claim: Al-Nuʿman ibn Bashir reports the Prophet saying supplication is worship and then reciting this verse; no grading is stated.
THALABI:v8p280/r5.anchor: عن النعمان بن بشير قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «الدعاء هو العبادة

THALABI:v8p280/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p280/r6.speaker: سفيان
THALABI:v8p280/r6.claim: When asked to pray for him, Sufyan answered that abandoning sins is itself supplication.
THALABI:v8p280/r6.anchor: قيل لسفيان: ادع الله. قال: إن ترك الذنوب هو الدعاء

THALABI:v8p280/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p280/r7.speaker: ابن كثير
THALABI:v8p280/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Jaʿfar, and Abu Hatim read the verb passively, with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on khāʾ; the source notes disagreement among other readers.
THALABI:v8p280/r7.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو جعفر وأبو حاتم: بضم الياء وفتح الخاء.

THALABI:v8p280/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p280/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو وعاصم
THALABI:v8p280/r8.claim: The source reports disagreement about this reading from Abu Amr and Asim and others, without clearly assigning each alternative in the excerpt.
THALABI:v8p280/r8.anchor: عن أبي عمرو وعاصم غير هم ضده

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:60/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:60/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:60/r1.claim: The command to call on God means to worship Him, for which He will reward and forgive them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:60/r1.anchor: ادعوني أستجب لكم } اعبدوني أثبكم وأغفر لكم

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r11.speaker: Ibn Abbas, Dahhâk ve Mücâhid
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r11.claim: One interpretation takes “call on Me” as worship Me and “I will answer” as grant reward; on this view, practical striving is also required.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r11.anchor: İbn Abbas, Dahhâk ve Mücâhid’den mervî olan

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r12.speaker: Süddî
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r12.claim: A second interpretation, transmitted from Suddi and apparent at first glance, is “ask Me and I will give you,” with worship then understood as prayer.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r12.anchor: ve ilk nazarda anlaşılan da budur.

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r13.claim: The two readings emphasize that prayer and worship entail one another: prayer is worship’s core, while worship is among the conditions for prayer’s acceptance.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r13.anchor: Bunu böyle iki vecihli olarak ifadenin nüktesi, ibadetin dua

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r14.claim: The command to ask establishes particular human will and rejects compulsion; asking is a condition of God’s response, and abandoning the command incurs the threat of Hell.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r14.anchor: Gerek ibadet mânasına olsun gerek sade dua, ikisinde de istemek emredilmiş

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r15.claim: The promise does not mean every prayer is necessarily answered; acceptance is qualified by God’s will, as 6:41 states.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r15.anchor: meşiyyet ile mukayyeddir. Yani buradan anlaşılan kaziyye-i şartiye külliye değil mühmeledir.

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r16.claim: The condition is not a universally quantified promise, and acceptance also depends on conditions such as good words and righteous deeds in 35:10.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r16.anchor: Müeddâsınca bazı şerâit-i kabul ile de meşruttur.

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r17.speaker: Ka‘b
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r17.claim: Al-Kashshaf transmits Ka‘b’s report that this community received three privileges: witness over humanity, freedom from hardship, and the promise “call on Me and I will answer,” linked to 2:143, 33:38, and 5:6.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r17.anchor: Keşşâf da Ka‘b’dan şöyle nakleder: Allah teâlâ bu ümmete üç haslet vermiştir ki onları nebiyy-i mürsel olanlardan başkasına vermemişti

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r18.claim: “Call Me” may mean seek Me from Me: God answers by being found, and whoever finds God has found everything, since all things obey His creative command in 36:82.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r18.anchor: Benden Beni talep edin, size icâbet ederim, Beni bulursunuz, Beni bulan da her şeyi bulmuş olur.

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r19.claim: Elmalılı says this God-seeking prayer is described as never rejected, and cites a report meaning “whoever seeks Me finds Me.”
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r19.anchor: Denilmiştir ki işte hiç reddolunmayan dua budur.

ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r20.claim: Those who arrogantly refuse worship or seeking God through prayer remain humiliated and deprived in the Hell of separation from Him.
ELMALILI:40:56-60#3/r20.anchor: Bana ibadetten, yani Bana dua ile Beni

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r1.claim: The preceding passage rejects doubts about resurrection and the afterlife, says good and evil people are not equal, and affirms the coming Hour; this verse then calls disbelievers to salvation through faith and good works.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r1.anchor: Yukarıda inkârcıların, yeniden dirilme ve âhiret hayatı konusundaki kuşkuları reddedilmiş; bilginin cahillikle, iyi iş yapanların kötülük yapanlarla bir tutulamayacağı belirtilmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r2.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r2.claim: Tabari reads “call upon me” as worshipping God alone rather than idols, so that he accepts the prayer, shows mercy, and forgives; the verse’s following reference to worship supports this sense.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r2.anchor: Taberî, “Bana dua edin” buyruğunu, “Bana kulluk edin; ibadeti benden başkasına, putlara ve başka şeylere değil, sırf bana yapın ki duanızı kabul edeyim; size rahmetimle muamele edeyim ve sizi bağışlayayım” şeklinde açıklamıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r3.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r3.claim: The Prophet reportedly said that supplication is worship, then recited this verse; no grading is stated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r3.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in “Dua ibadetin kendisidir” buyurduğu, ardından da bu âyeti okuduğu bildirilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r4.speaker: Süfyân-ı Sevrî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r4.claim: Sufyan al-Thawri said that even refraining from sins counts as supplication.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r4.anchor: ünlü âlim Süfyân-ı Sevrî, günahlardan uzak durmanın bile dua olduğunu belirtmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r5.claim: The verse broadly calls disbelievers, beginning with its first hearers, to pray to God and receive his response.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r5.anchor: İşte âyette, başta Kur’an’ın ilk muhatapları olmak üzere inkârcılar, bu geniş anlamda Allah’a dua etmeye ve O’ndan karşılık almaya çağırılmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r6.claim: Those who arrogantly refuse the call, worship of God, and submission to the Prophet’s religion will enter Hell humiliated and disgraced.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:60/r6.anchor: hâlâ kör bir inatla büyüklük taslayıp Allah’a kulluk etmeyi ve Resûlullah’ın getirdiği dinin kurallarına teslim olmayı kendilerine yediremeyenlerin varacakları son yerin, zelil ve hakir vaziyette girecekleri cehennem olduğu haber verilmektedir

ITQAN:v2p329#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p329#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p329#2/r1.claim: The imperative udʿūnī is glossed as worship or affirm My oneness.

ITQAN:v4p527#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p527#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p527#2/r1.claim: The Prophet said that supplication is worship, then recited 40:60; the source names Ahmad, the Sunan compilers, al-Hakim, and Ibn Hibban without giving a grading.
ITQAN:v4p527#2/r1.anchor: أخرج أحمد وأصحاب السنن والحاكم وابن حبان عن النعمان بن بشير قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إن الدعاء هو العبادة ثم قرأ

ITQAN:v2p558/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p558/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p558/r2.claim: A relative clause can intend generality; this verse includes all who are arrogant about worship, alongside examples about those who profess God and persevere and those who strive for Him.
ITQAN:v2p558/r2.anchor: وقد يكون لإرادة العموم نحو ﴿ إن الذين قالوا ربنا الله ثم استقاموا ﴾ الآية ﴿ والذين جاهدوا فينا لنهدينهم سبلنا ﴾

ITQAN:v2p558/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p558/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p558/r4.claim: The definite article can point to something known externally, mentally, or in the present situation.
ITQAN:v2p558/r4.anchor: وبالألف واللام للإشارة إلى معهود خارجي أو ذهني أو حضوري

ITQAN:v2p558/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p558/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p558/r5.claim: The definite article can mark exhaustive inclusion literally or figuratively, or define a kind or genus.
ITQAN:v2p558/r5.anchor: وللإستغراق حقيقة أو مجازا أو لتعريف الماهية

ITQAN:v2p558/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p558/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p558/r6.claim: A genitive construction can be concise and can exalt what is possessed, as in God's servants; Ibn Abbas and others interpret both examples as referring to the elect.
ITQAN:v2p558/r6.anchor: وبالإضافة لكونها أخصر طريق ولتعظيم المضاف نحو ﴿ إن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان ﴾ ﴿ ولا يرضى لعباده الكفر ﴾

ITQAN:v2p558/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p558/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v2p558/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas and others gloss God's servants in the two cited verses as the elect or specially chosen servants.
ITQAN:v2p558/r7.anchor: أي الأصفياء في الآيتين كما قاله ابن عباس وغيره

ITQAN:v2p558/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p558/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p558/r8.claim: A genitive can express generality: believers are warned to heed every command of God in the cited verse.
ITQAN:v2p558/r8.anchor: ولقصد العموم نحو ﴿ فليحذر الذين يخالفون عن أمره ﴾ أي كل أمر الله تعالى

NAHHAS:v4p38/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p38/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p38/r12.claim: Basrans treat ادعوني as an uninflected imperative unless lām accompanies it; al-Farra makes it jussive by deleted lām, while أستجب is jussive as a conditional response.
NAHHAS:v4p38/r12.anchor: ادعوني أمر غير معرب ولا مجزوم عند البصريين إلا أن تكون معه اللام وعند الفراء مجزوم على حذف اللام

NAHHAS:v4p38/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p38/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p38/r13.claim: The hamza in أستجب is قطع like the nūn in نفعل; hamzat al-wasl drops because it is unnecessary.
NAHHAS:v4p38/r13.anchor: وهذه الهمزة مقطوعة لأنها بمنزلة النون في نفعل وسقطت ألف الوصل لأنه قد استغني عنها

TABATABAI:2:21-25#18/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#18/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#18/r4.claim: The open-ended promises that God answers supplication and suffices His servant reinforce that ordinary causal expectations do not limit what God brings about.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#18/r4.anchor: كما يدل عليه أيضا إطلاق قوله تعالى

NASHR:v2p164/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p164/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p164/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr alone opens two yāʾs: فاذكروني أذكركم in al-Baqara and ادعوني أستجب لكم in Ghāfir.
NASHR:v2p164/r2.anchor: فاختص ابن كثير بفتح ياءين منها، وهما فاذكروني أذكركم

NASHR:v2p365/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p365/r6.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v2p365/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir opens the yāʾ in ادعوني أستجب.

RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r1.claim: A second proof of prayer's excellence is God's command to call upon Him with a promise to answer.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85/r1.anchor: الحجة الثانية في فضل الدعاء : قوله تعالى : { وقال ربكم ادعونى أستجب لكم }

RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r4.claim: Although promises to answer prayer appear unqualified in these verses, Razi says a further verse qualifies them: God removes what is invoked only if He wills, and the general wording is read in light of that qualification.
RAZI-FULL:v5p85#2/r4.anchor: بل إياه تدعون فيكشف ما تدعون إليه إن شاء
